english_translation: The river is flowing with strong currents, so do not cross.

dialogue.shona: Rwizi rwuri kuyerera zvine simba saka musayambuke.
dialogue.english: The river is flowing with strong currents, so do not cross.
dialogue.literal_gloss: Rwizi [river] • rwuri [rwuri] • kuyerera [to / at yerera] • zvine [things ne] • simba [simba] • saka [so / therefore] • musayambuke [in / singular sayambuke]

grammar_notes.title: Actions Happening Right Now: The '-ri ku-' Progressive
grammar_notes.content: To describe an action that is happening right now ('I am doing', 'it is raining', 'they are walking'), Shona uses the helper verb '-ri' ('am/is/are') followed by 'ku-' ('to') and the action verb. For people, the forms are 'ndiri ku-' (I am), 'uri ku-' (you are), 'ari ku-' (he/she is), 'tiri ku-' (we are), and 'vari ku-' (they are). In fast speech or writing, the two words are sometimes joined together (e.g., 'ndiri kuenda' or 'ndirikuenda').
grammar_notes.rule: [Subject + -ri] + ku-[verb] -> Ndiri kuverenga (I am reading) | Vari kufamba (They are walking) | Mvura iri kunaya (It is raining)

grammar_notes.title: Infinitive Verbs & Action Nouns with 'ku-' ('kuyerera')
grammar_notes.content: Look at 'kuyerera' in this sentence. Every Shona verb in its dictionary ('to do') form begins with 'ku-': for example, 'kudya' (to eat), 'kutenga' (to buy), 'kubhadhara' (to pay), 'kuona' (to see), and 'kurwa' (to fight). Because 'ku-' verbs also behave as action nouns ('eating', 'paying', 'working'), you can attach linking prefixes directly to them: 'yekubhadhara' ('for paying'), 'pakubikwa' ('in the cooking'), and 'nekuona' ('by/with seeing').
grammar_notes.rule: ku- + Verb Stem = 'to [verb] / [verb]-ing' (ku- + -tenga = kutenga, 'to buy'; ye- + kubhadhara = yekubhadhara, 'for paying')

grammar_notes.title: Linking Ideas Smoothly with 'saka'
grammar_notes.content: Longer Shona sentences flow naturally by linking two clauses with connectors like 'saka'. The four essential connectors to master are: 'uye' ('and / furthermore' between two clauses), 'asi' ('but / however'), 'saka' ('so / therefore'), and 'nokuti' / 'nekuti' ('because').

cultural_notes.title: Flooded Rivers ('Rwizi Rwuri Kuyerera Zvine Simba') in the Rainy Season
cultural_notes.content: During heavy summer rains, Zimbabwe's seasonal and perennial rivers swell rapidly with powerful currents ('kuyerera zvine simba'). Elders and safety campaigns always warn travellers: 'Musayambuke rwizi rwuzere!' ('Never cross a flooded river!').

active_exercises.prompt: If a farmer says 'Gore rino takawana goho guru pamunda pedu', what happened?
options: They are waiting for the rain to start next month
The river flooded and washed away the bridge
A strong wind blew from the east all afternoon
They obtained a big harvest from their field this year
active_exercises.correct_answer: They obtained a big harvest from their field this year
active_exercises.explanation: 'Takawana' = 'we obtained/got', 'goho guru' = 'a big harvest', 'pamunda pedu' = 'from our field'.

active_exercises.prompt: Translate this new sentence into English: 'Mhepo iri kuvhuvhuta uye mvura ichanaya manheru.'
options: The wind is blowing and it will rain in the evening.
The river is full of water after yesterday's heavy rain.
Tall green trees grow along the sides of the mountain.
The dog barked outside when it saw the visitors.
active_exercises.correct_answer: The wind is blowing and it will rain in the evening.
active_exercises.explanation: 'Mhepo iri kuvhuvhuta' = 'The wind is blowing', 'uye' = 'and', 'mvura ichanaya manheru' = 'it will rain in the evening'.

active_exercises.prompt: Your friend just passed her driving test! What do you say to congratulate her in Shona?
active_exercises.explanation: 'Makorokoto!' means 'Congratulations!' and 'nekubudirira kwako' means 'on your success'.
